transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-16
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE); Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE); Sasha Ivanov (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (NexaHead ML); Evan Li (Nexa Platform); Anita Gomez (Nexa Security); Leo Carter (Nexa Data)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's runs, access gaps, and next steps to run full benchmark and handoff infra.

00:00 Jamie Park: ok everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight 45 minutes, main goals  check results from your sample runs, see what infra access is left, and agree next steps for the larger benchmark
00:18 Priya Shah: yep thanks jamie, we ran the sample across about 2k clinical notes last thursday, so we have some initial latency and cost numbers, want to get clarity on, um, the dedicated profile you suggested
00:33 Carlos Mendez: great, thanks Priya. quick note  i'm Carlos, I'll own the benchmark side. quick preface: last week's test used our hosted endpoint with a small batch setting (batch size 8, kv cache off for that run) so numbers are expected to be a little worse than dedicated. i captured the logs and put a short spreadsheet link in the chat  (see drive: /redwood/poc/nexa/bench-2027-02-09)
01:02 Leo Carter: i saw that; for some rows the tokens-per-call are off, i think the transcription split merged two messages, so counts look high, but overall latency p95 looks around 420-480ms
01:17 Carlos Mendez: yeah there's some transcribe noise, but corrected numbers i have  p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 450ms for hosted on our standard plan, cost around $0.012 per 1k tokens for that model variant. again that's without kv cache and without quantized model.
01:38 Priya Shah: could you remind us which model variant that is? last meeting i thought it was the rdx-3b-ish?
01:45 Carlos Mendez: right we've been using rdx-3b-v2 (open-variant) as baseline. for Dedicated we expect p95 to drop to ~280-320ms and unit cost to decline by about 25-35% depending on batching and kv cache usage.
02:02 Evan Li: ok that matches our target; our SLA for feature is p95 under 350ms so if dedicated hits 280-320ms that's promising. our main worry is overhead for VPC peering and key management  Anita will chime in there.
02:18 Anita Gomez: yep security first. quick list  we need SOC2 or equivalent, audit log retention controls, SSO (SAML) metadata, and the KMS/HSM integration details. also we need to know what data leaves our VPC during hosted runs vs dedicated/private.
02:36 Jamie Park: totally  we have a security pack that includes SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, and our audit logging spec. i'll share that after the call. for KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration and for Private deployments HSM is supported  for Dedicated there's an option for customer-key integration; i'll let Carlos elaborate on the exact flow.
02:55 Carlos Mendez: short version: for hosted we store minimal logs, customer data can be configured to not be persisted; for Dedicated or Private we can set up customer key integration so keys remain in your KMS and logs are limited to control-plane events. i will attach the diagram  small caveat in the diagram the term 'kv cache' got spelled 'k-v cash' in the auto doc  typical transcription weirdness.
03:16 Priya Shah: ha noted. about access  Evan mentioned peering window, are we still missing any pieces to spin up the dedicated-like environment for benchmark?
03:26 Evan Li: we need two things: 1) CIDR block for Redwood to peer, and 2) a service account with least privilege to fetch from our bench bucket (the dataset). also we want to avoid giving blanket access to internal prod logs.
03:39 Carlos Mendez: understood. our recommended flow: set up VPC peering with a restrictive CIDR, create a bench IAM role with read-only to the S3-like bucket, and provide SAML metadata so we can do admin console testing. we'll follow your security constraints.
03:58 Anita Gomez: also can you confirm audit log retention options  we need 12 months of immutable logs for our compliance team.
04:08 Carlos Mendez: yes we support 12-month retention in the Enterprise plan; for Dedicated we can enable append-only logs shipped to your bucket. will include that in the security pack.
04:22 Leo Carter: quick question on quantization  last run used float16, is there a recommended quantized profile to lower cost without sacrificing accuracy on clinical notes?
04:34 Carlos Mendez: good q. our Optimize toolkit suggests q4_0 or q5_x for 3B-ish models; for clinical notes i'd recommend q4_0 with a small eval on 1k records to validate quality. that usually gives ~30-40% token cost reduction, sometimes more with batching.
04:58 Priya Shah: and can Redwood run that eval or do we need to run locally?
05:04 Carlos Mendez: we can run both  we can run a Dedicated-like eval on our infra (with masked PHI) if you provide a de-identified sample; alternatively your team can run the same script we provide. for speed we'll run it if you can confirm dataset pointer and access.
05:20 Evan Li: we'll provide a de-id sample and an IAM role. timeline  can you complete the 10k benchmark and quant eval by end of next week?
05:30 Carlos Mendez: yes aiming for 2027-02-19. that's what Carlos will own.
05:35 Sasha Ivanov: i'll coordinate scheduling for the infra handoff call, want to include your infra and our infra ops; propose 60 minute window for peering and key exchange.
05:46 Priya Shah: sounds good. one more question  our procurement wants to understand pricing delta between hosted and dedicated for this pilot. can you send a provisional sheet?
05:55 Jamie Park: yes i'll send the pricing spreadsheet and call out assumptions (commit size, burst policy, quantization assumptions). i put a link in chat to the pricing doc (drive: /redwood/poc/nexa/pricing-v2.xlsx).
06:09 Anita Gomez: on legal  we may need a data processing addendum (DPA) and export controls note; can you confirm if Redwood has a standard DPA?
06:18 Jamie Park: yes standard DPA is available, i'll include that in the security pack. for export controls i'll get the legal team to confirm and include the short note.
06:30 Leo Carter: small nit  in the bench spreadsheet some samples show higher latency when context length > 1k tokens; is that expected?
06:38 Carlos Mendez: yes expected. the runtime kernel selection and memory pressure make long-context calls heavier. for those we typically recommend dynamic kernel selection and enabling prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated context. we'll evaluate that in the benchmark config.
06:55 Priya Shah: ok let's recap next steps  who is doing what?
07:02 Jamie Park: recap: Carlos runs 10k benchmark + quant eval (due 2027-02-19), Evan provides CIDR + bench IAM role (due 2027-02-18), Anita provides compliance doc list and SSO metadata (due 2027-02-20), Jamie sends security pack & pricing (due 2027-02-17). schedule infra handoff (Sasha to coordinate).
07:30 Priya Shah: perfect  schedule the follow-up after results, tentatively 2027-02-23. thanks everyone.
07:45 Jamie Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and share the results + call notes.
